name: Phosphate
rangeNote: Children and teenagers normally have higher phosphate, so this adult range starts at age 20. Phosphate also changes with meals and time of day. A sample that was damaged or left standing before it reached the lab can read falsely high.
summary: Phosphate is a mineral that, with calcium, builds bones and teeth. Every cell also uses it to store and move energy. Labs may call it phosphorus; it is the same test.

high.meaning: A high phosphate is most often linked to reduced kidney function, because the kidneys remove extra phosphate. In long-term kidney disease, a lasting high level is linked to calcium deposits in blood vessels. A single high result can also come from the sample itself.
commonCauses: Damaged blood sample (haemolysis) or a delay before testing

low.meaning: A mildly low phosphate often causes no symptoms. A very low level can cause muscle weakness and, rarely, breathing or heart problems. It matters most when the body's stores are also low.
commonCauses: Eating again after a long period of very little food (refeeding)
